transcript: Do recruiters only read a resume for 7 seconds? Yeah, sometimes. But the reason is because it's pretty easy to eliminate a lot of resumes in that amount of time. Resumes that need to be read for more time are read for more time. Let me show you where my eyes go when I open a resume. Keeping in mind there is nothing more important than the experience on a resume. It has to match up with the job. When I open a resume like this with nothing but buzzwords and a long summary, I don't read it because I know there's nothing individualized in there. I go right down here to the experience. I can quickly get a feel for what this person was doing and this is aligned. If I'm looking for a software engineer, this person's out. I don't need to read it for more than 7 seconds. But I will dig in after this. You can also get me to keep reading by telling me immediately at the top what you need me to know and how it aligns with the job I'm looking for. Doing that combined with a summary that's very specific to you versus generic summary can do a lot. This is likely going to make me keep reading if I'm looking for a marketing director with demand gen experience. It's not about the order or the specific sections. It's about how quickly can I see what I need to see.
